title: Finite pinching reduction and state-weighted shell commutator bound
question: Can the FI-2b bond commutator be reduced exactly to the coordinate-off-diagonal part of a centered doubled collision witness, with a reference-weighted Cauchy bound that introduces no dimension or volume factor?

theorem.setting: A finite doubled Hilbert space with faithful reference state omega=rho tensor rho, a coordinate basis and its dephasing conditional expectation E_D, a Hermitian coordinate-diagonal bond generator B, and any witness X.
theorem.finite_scope: The identity and bound are finite-dimensional; their constants are exactly 1 at the Cauchy step, but no cutoff, volume, prefix, source or exhaustion uniformity follows.

verification_contract.lean_scope: finite coordinate dephasing/off-diagonal commutator identity and scalar-centering invariance

promotion_boundary: R-363 closes only the finite conditional-expectation reduction and its state-weighted Cauchy bound. FI-2b remains open until the off-diagonal weighted norms are controlled uniformly for every source, cutoff, volume, prefix and allowed exhaustion shape.
next_action: Measure the off-diagonal weighted norms along increasing cutoffs and volumes; seek a local modular or Lieb-Robinson estimate, and register a scoped growth obstruction if the normalized bound diverges.
boundary: Finite exact algebra plus finite V=2 Q3 diagnostics. No uniform local collar, phase-weight theorem, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
no_overclaim: The pinching identity removes diagonal bond contributions exactly and the Cauchy constant is one; it does not show that the remaining off-diagonal witness norm is uniformly bounded.
